speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help me understand the extent of this issue, could you tell me when these symptoms first started? Also, has this weakness spread to your shoulder or down into your hand?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the progressive weakness, significant weight loss, and your history of smoking and steroid use, this raises concern for a malignancy such as Pancoast tumor or lymphoma affecting the brachial plexus. Can you describe exactly where you feel the numbness or pain, and is there any swelling or lumps you can feel in your neck, shoulder, or upper chest?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor)
